Best CCTV and Security Companies in Kuching for a Small Business Upgrade

Three Kuching options for combining surveillance with front-desk systems, planning maintenance or sourcing specific equipment.

Eyonic Sdn Bhd for a CCTV upgrade that includes a staffed reception

Eyonic is my first pick on this list if you're planning new CCTV for a Kuching workplace and want to discuss the reception phone system with the same local provider. Eyonic publishes separate service pages for CCTV and for keyphone and PABX, and its CCTV page describes planning, supply and installation for homes, businesses and industrial sites. Its official contact page lists a Kuching office in Heights Drive Commercial Centre. The reason to start here is the way those published capabilities fit this particular brief. Actual site coverage, equipment, lead time and responsibility for any existing system should be confirmed in the quote.

Eyonic’s PABX and keyphone services

Consider a fictional shop with a rear goods entrance, two counters and a shared reception desk. The owner wants a clearer record of deliveries and a way for staff upstairs to answer calls when the front desk is busy. Ask Eyonic to walk through those as two jobs with an agreed handover. The first needs a clear description of what each proposed camera is meant to show. The second needs an explanation of how a call moves between staff. Ask what can be reused and what comes separately so that neither system gets lost in a single price line.

Blackstone Intelligence prepared this comparison and features Eyonic first. Public service pages and supplier information were reviewed on 27 November 2026. This is a shortlist for a particular requirement. I have not commissioned installations, compared current prices or independently tested the companies' work.

eyonicsecuritysystem.com.my

In a shared commercial unit, take a copy of the tenancy or building instructions to the walkthrough. Ask who is authorised to approve work in shared corridors and where the installer can run cables. A clear boundary helps you compare quotes based on the same rooms and entrances instead of paying for a plan the building manager has yet to approve.

HJ Security for a maintenance or wider integration comparison

HJ Security's corporate website lists CCTV, alarms, door access, autogates, Wi-Fi and related building systems. Its website separates requests for new installations from service and maintenance for existing systems. Start there if you already have equipment that needs assessment or if you want a second proposal for an upgrade with several connected systems. Ask what the first assessment covers and whether the support agreement is included or offered separately.

HJ Security’s published service information

A useful enquiry gives the team the age of the equipment if known, a description of the symptoms and which parts of the system still work. If the problem only happens at a certain time, describe when staff have noticed it. Ask HJ to list the areas that require on-site confirmation before making a proposal, so you can distinguish their estimated scope from agreed work.

Saxco Marketing Kuching for equipment research and supply

Saxco Marketing presents itself as a distributor of security products, and its official product material lists a Kuching outlet. It is the relevant comparison here when someone on your team is trying to identify a replacement model or understand what is available to buy. Confirm the installation and after-sales arrangements for the specific item directly. A product catalogue by itself cannot establish who will assess a site, handle cabling or support work done there.

Saxco Marketing’s CCTV equipment guide

For example, if a contractor has asked you to buy a replacement camera, request the exact compatibility requirements in writing before talking to the supplier. Then check who owns the commissioning step after purchase and who handles a return if the delivered item differs from the model ordered. This keeps equipment supply and installation responsibility easy to compare.

A short walkthrough before you ask for pricing

Walk the premises with the people who actually open and close it. Write a one-line description of each event you need to review, such as a delivery arriving, a customer waiting for service or a staff member needing to answer a call from another room. Use those events to guide the discussion with installers. Documenting the event is more useful at this stage than picking a camera count or a phone model from a catalogue.

For mixed-use premises, identify the decision maker early. If the owner approves building changes and the tenant runs the front desk, ask who will sign off cable routes, view access and the location of equipment. Keep a note of which parts may require coordination with a building manager. Agree privately who is allowed to view recorded material and who can add or remove users. A good quote should explain the provider's role in setting up the system and where your own responsibilities begin.

Describe any downtime constraints. A Kuching shop that opens early may need different phasing from an office that can free up a meeting room in the afternoon. Ask each provider to state what normally needs access and for how long it expects to affect operations. For a multi-site owner adding Miri or Bintulu, confirm travel and support arrangements for each premises instead of using the Kuching schedule as a proxy.

What should be written into the handover

Ask for a demonstration in terms your staff can repeat. For CCTV, that might mean finding footage from a specified date and explaining who can access it. For the keyphone system, it might mean receiving a call at the front desk and transferring it to the correct team. Write the demonstration into the scope before work begins. The point is to agree on what is meant by finished while everyone can still ask for clarification.

Then compare the proposals using three lines: what equipment is supplied, what work is included and what support applies afterward. Distinguish a defect in a delivered item from a problem with an existing system. Ask whether a return visit is included to resolve questions from the first week or whether all changes after sign-off are priced separately. A short written explanation today makes the first support call easier later.

Eyonic is the best fit on this shortlist for a small commercial project that puts CCTV and reception calling in the same brief. HJ Security is a sensible second conversation when maintaining existing systems is central. Saxco is useful when you need a supplier comparison for specified equipment. Take the same description of your site to each provider that fits and compare what they'll put in writing.
